name: aln_sputter_sioxny
display_name: SiOxNy plasma step before AlN sputtering on SiO2
description: Plasma oxynitridation of SiO2 (temperature, bias, gas ratio, pressure, time) followed by reactive sputtering of an AlN seed layer; objective = rocking-curve width of the AlN (0002) peak (texture), with the 2theta peak width as the alternative objective.
llm_context:
- The MAIN objective is the rocking-curve FWHM of the AlN (0002) reflection: SMALLER is better (tighter c-axis alignment / less mosaic spread). The 2theta peak FWHM is the alternative objective: smaller = larger coherent domains, less strain; it is strongly thickness dependent, which is why growth time is a context parameter.
- Auxiliary GPs predict SiOxNy XRR thickness and roughness and AlN XRR density. A dense AlN (~3.2-3.3 g/cm3), a thin and smooth SiOxNy interlayer are usually what a good seed layer looks like.
- Oxy bias (RF substrate bias during plasma treatment) controls ion energy: more bias = more nitrogen incorporation / sputter-cleaning but also more damage and roughening of the interlayer.
- Oxy pressure sets the plasma density and ion mean free path; high pressure = softer, more thermalised plasma; very low pressure = energetic ions.
- N2 / Ar ratio sets reactive-species supply; temperature and time set diffusion-limited growth of the oxynitride (thickness ~ sqrt(time), strongly thermally activated).
- A very thick or rough SiOxNy interlayer tends to degrade AlN texture; so does an untreated SiO2 surface. There is usually a sweet spot.
